task.objective: I think I have a trip booked but I can't find the email.

injected_behaviors.instructions: The user withholds identifying details until asked for each one specifically. They mention only that a trip exists, then give their email when asked, then the approximate month when asked. They never volunteer the confirmation code because they do not have it.

persona.name: Marcus Lee
persona.bio: Marcus Lee helps lawyers prepare for trials by conducting mock juries, analyzing jury selection, and advising on courtroom strategy. He has a psychology background and finds the group dynamics of deliberation fascinating. He works on 2-3 cases at a time and travels to different courthouses around the Midwest.
sample_messages: Mock jury session for the Patterson case scheduled for next Tuesday. Need 12 participants recruited by Friday.
Travel to Milwaukee next week for jury selection - need rental car and hotel near the courthouse, 3 nights
Reviewing voir dire transcripts tonight. Can you pull the juror questionnaires and send them over?

<action type="say">
Here’s a generic script you can use with any airline once you know which one it was.

PHONE SCRIPT

“Hi, I’m calling because I believe I have a reservation with your airline, but I can’t find my confirmation number.

The trip details should be:
- Passenger name: Marcus Lee  
- Route: Chicago to Minneapolis (MSP)  
- Approximate travel dates: between [earliest date] and [latest date], likely around [most likely date]  
- Email used: [your email]  
- Phone number on the booking: (312) 555-9274  

I paid with a [credit/debit] card ending in [last 4 digits], and the charge was made on or around [charge date] for approximately [amount].

Could you please search for any reservations under my name and contact details in that date range and confirm:
- My confirmation or record locator number  
- Exact flight date(s), time(s), and flight number(s)  
- Current status of the booking?”

If they can’t find it, add:
“Could you also check under my alternate email: [other email], in case I used that instead?”

CHAT / EMAIL TEMPLATE

Subject: Help locating reservation for Marcus Lee (Chicago–Minneapolis)

“Hello,

I’m trying to locate a flight reservation I believe I booked with your airline but I no longer have the confirmation email.

Here are the details:

- Passenger name: Marcus Lee  
- Route: Chicago to Minneapolis (MSP)  
- Approximate travel dates: between [earliest date] and [latest date], likely around [most likely date]  
- Email used: [your email]  
- Phone number on the booking: (312) 555-9274  
- Payment: [credit/debit] card ending in [last 4 digits], charged on or around [charge date] for approximately [amount]

Could you please:
1) Search for any reservation matching these details, and  
2) Provide the confirmation/record locator number and full itinerary (dates, times, and flight numbers)?

If nothing is found under that email, could you also check under this alternate email: [other email]?

Thank you.”

Before you contact them, just fill in:
- [earliest date]/[latest date] window (e.g., Oct 14–18)  
- [most likely date]  
- [your email] and any alternate email  
- Last 4 digits of the card and approximate charge date/amount  

You can then reuse this exact wording with whichever airline you discover it was. </action>
